To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

our algorithm is a new algorithm for continuous batch reinforcement learning that outperforms the state of the art in all benchmarks, and that it can learn good policies from offline data without requiring any online interaction with the environment.

(1) batch reinforcement learning is a challenging problem that requires careful treatment of uncertainty, (2) we propose an approach that is able to learn effective policies using only offline data, (3) the approach is able to learn good policies even when the training data was collected using different policies than the ones we are learning, and (4) our approach is able to outperform state-of-the-art baselines in a comprehensive set of benchmarks.

(1) we introduce a new algorithm for batch RL with continuous action spaces, (2) the algorithm combines policy and value constraints to improve extrapolation in value estimation, (3) the algorithm performs well on a wide variety of benchmarks, (4) the algorithm is competitive with the state-of-the-art on all but one of the $32$ benchmark environments
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of learning to solve sequential decision making tasks from a fixed batch of data.

the problem of learning a policy that optimizes the cumulative reward in a given Markov decision process (MDP), when the MDP is not fully known and the agent is only able to interact with the environment through trial-and-error.

the problem of batch reinforcement learning, where we aim at learning an effective policy using an offline dataset of past interactions with the environment, rather than by interacting with the environment.

simple constraints can help to learn effective batch RL policies.
